title: Crypto-Asset Service Providers and Business Models
summary: The roles, activities and business models of crypto-asset service providers, how they make money, and how to determine which licences and registrations a business needs.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The roles, activities and business models of crypto-asset service providers, how they make money, and how to determine which licences and registrations a business needs.
Learning Objectives: Identify core service provider activities and services
Analyse business models, revenue sources and unit economics in crypto markets
Determine the perimeter, licensing and registration needs of a business
Syllabus: Exchanges, brokers and trading platforms: operating structures
Custodians, wallet providers, issuers and token platforms
Hybrid and decentralised models: perimeter and licensing implications
Intended Audience: Founders, senior managers and staff of crypto-asset service providers, issuers and fintech firms, and of banks, asset managers and payment firms entering digital assets
Compliance, risk, MLRO, legal, operations and product professionals working on digital asset activities
Consultants, lawyers, auditors, investors and other advisers who support crypto-asset businesses
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial services, compliance, risk or advisory work is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
Basel Committee, Prudential Treatment of Cryptoasset Exposures (2022)
